title: Export fingerprinting and partial-day proration rewrite for accurate invoice attribution
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem:
Current billing export and reconciler produce non-deterministic invoice lines for mid-cycle usage adjustments and partial-day plan changes. Multiple failure modes observed: (1) duplicate credit/charge lines when late-usage backfills hit the export window, (2) inconsistent proration rounding across Stripe and NetSuite leading to small cents-level drift, and (3) inability to idempotently re-run export jobs because there is no stable export signature per invoice line.

Goal:
Implement a deterministic export fingerprint for every export line and rewrite the partial-day proration logic to anchor on an hourly-anchored, timezone-aware window. The fingerprint+new proration will: (a) make export lines idempotent and dedupable across retries and replays, (b) consolidate mid-cycle adjustments into a small number of canonical lines to prevent invoice wobble, and (c) provide metadata for automatic anomaly detection in downstream NetSuite imports.

High-level approach:
- Add export_fingerprint: sha256(customer_id + billing_window_start_utc + meter_key + allocation_bucket + proration_scheme + export_schema_version) encoded hex. This is written with each raw export line and used by the reconciler to detect duplicates and stable merges.
- Replace current pro-rata-by-second approach with a "partial-day anchored to hour" algorithm: quantize plan-change intervals into hour buckets using the customer's billing timezone, compute fractional day weight as sum(bucket_weights)/24 with configurable rounding policy (banker's rounding for cents).
- Update the reconciler to prefer merging lines that share fingerprint family and to emit a single canonical line per family with deterministic aggregation rules (sum of amounts, earliest timestamp, max taxonomy tags).
- Produce a per-export checksum (signed HMAC) so downstream consumers can validate export integrity before NetSuite ingest.

Why different from previous fixes:
Previous fixes patched edge cases (DST, late webhook retries) but did not introduce a stable identifier for exports, so replay-detection remained brittle. This change introduces an explicit fingerprint and aggregation rules, enabling safe replays and simpler downstream import logic.
acceptance_criteria: Export lines include stable export_fingerprint and export_schema_version
Reconciler deduplicates repeated export runs: running same input twice should not create duplicate NetSuite lines
Partial-day invoicing for plan switches within a calendar day is within +/- $0.05 cents of golden reference for 99.9% of test cases (covering DST, timezone edge cases)
Automated backfill of 7 days of late-usage does not create more than one correction line per customer per day
End-to-end test that simulates webhook reorder and retry results in idempotent Stripe invoice outcomes
migration_plan: Phase 0: Feature-flag export_fingerprint generation in staging only
Phase 1: Run dual-writes (old export format + new fingerprinted format) for 72h and compare diffs using export-diff tooling
Phase 2: Flip reconciler to prefer fingerprint families for merge decisions in staging; validate NetSuite sandbox imports
Phase 3: Run a controlled production rollout (1% accounts -> 10% -> 50%) with automated anomaly gating on invoice variance and export line counts
Phase 4: If stable for 7 days, deprecate old format and enable in all accounts
rollout_plan: Enable for internal billing customers and monitoring dashboards first
Add automated gates: net-new export line delta, cents-drift per-invoice, reconciler merge rate
Incrementally increase percentage by manual approval after gates pass
Post-rollout: schedule a 2-week observation window and a rollback playbook
test_plan: Unit tests for SHA256 fingerprint composition and export_schema_version compatibility
Property tests: run randomized usage events + plan changes and assert deterministic fingerprinting and canonical aggregation
Integration tests: staging NetSuite import smoke test (sandbox), Stripe invoice idempotency validation
Backfill dry-run: run backfill job against last 30 days with dual-write diff reporting
Load test: ensure export job throughput meets SLA (no >10% latency regression)
Create a small cohort of real customers for canary with feature flag and monitor billing dashboards
risks: Incorrect fingerprint composition could cause unintended merges across distinct adjustments - mitigated by schema versioning and canarying
Rounding policy change may cause transient invoice diffs that large customers flag - mitigate by pre-notification and manual overrides
NetSuite import mappings may reject canonical merged lines if expected reference IDs are missing - mitigated by including legacy_ids in export metadata during dual-write
Rolling this change without traffic shaping could spike reconciler CPU due to additional hashing - mitigate by batching and incremental rollout
